definitions.explanation: An informal, slightly dismissive way to refer to a group of people. Can be neutral or carry a mildly negative or contemptuous nuance depending on context.

examples.japanese: あの{連中|れんちゅう}は{信用|しんよう}できない。
いつもの{連中|れんちゅう}で{飲|の}みに{行|い}った。
examples.english: I went out drinking with the usual crowd.

examples.japanese: あの{連中|れんちゅう}と{付|つ}き{合|あ}っていると、ろくなことがないよ。
examples.english: Nothing good will come from hanging around with that crowd.

notes:
USAGE:
{連中|れんちゅう} is informal and can range from casually neutral to dismissive or contemptuous depending on tone and context. It is not used in polite or formal speech.

When used about one's own group of friends, it is casual and friendly. When used about others, it often carries a negative or distancing nuance.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {仲間|なかま} — companions, friends (positive, warm)
- {一味|いちみ} — gang, accomplices (negative, criminal association)
- {連中|れんちゅう} — sits between these: informal, potentially dismissive

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- あの{連中|れんちゅう} (that bunch/crowd)
- いつもの{連中|れんちゅう} (the usual crowd)
- {役所|やくしょ}の{連中|れんちゅう} (the bureaucrats, those office people)
